segments.expected: She was on a ferry in the middle of a brown river, with a hand on her wrist and a voice counting. There was no roof. There were roads, and lights on them, a great many, coming from every side, and some of them were bright and some of them were dull. Some of them were going out. Some of them had gone white. She had been lower than she had ever been, near enough to see that some had gone white. She had not told anybody. She had not told Mara.

segments.expected: "Miss Rowan. Forgive me. I've been chasing you round the town since breakfast like a bailiff." He put his hat on. "I've two things to say, and one of them isn't mine. I'll say that one first, because I was asked to."
